text:
The provided abstract describes a **review article** that outlines the strengths and limitations of conventional and novel (microfluidic) strategies for EV isolation, surveys commercially available exosome isolation techniques and kits, and assesses global market demand for exosome assays.

In contrast, the candidate hypothesis proposes a highly specific experimental platform—a thermosensitive and pH-responsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-butyl methacrylate-co-N-hydroxysuccinimide methacrylate) (PNB) hydrogel covalently modified with aptamers against CD63 and CD81 for isolating exosomes from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) under specific temperature (30°C–37°C) and pH (6.5–7.5) conditions, integrated with SERS and advanced fluorescence characterization.

None of these specific materials, markers, cell sources, operating conditions, or characterization techniques appear in the abstract, nor does the review study provide evidence supporting such an experimental hypothesis.

VERDICT: REJECT
